propositions: The current per-criterion fan-out recovery explodes token cost (22 criteria × 20 requests = 440 worst case) and wall-clock time; the primary run's verified work is discarded on failure and recovery dies verdict-less when it exhausts.

A banked incremental verification design records criterion verdicts within the primary run and resumes unverified remainder in batched successor runs under a request budget pool, eliminating per-criterion fan-out and preserving partial progress.

Criterion identity is deterministically minted at run start and keyed in a run-scoped git-ignored bank; successors re-resolve ticket/material/tree stamps and fail loud on mismatch, enabling safe incremental progress.

The criteria-scaled step floor verify_step_floor(c) = clamp(8c, 48, 480) replaces the flat 480-step ceiling; empirically a typical ticket converges without recovery, reducing the frequency recovery is triggered.
Read-file memo is normalized by path to cache whole-file content once and serve all ranges from cache, collapsing the dominant 77% re-read tax during verification.

A finalizer with deterministic no-LLM fallback and downgrade authority ensures full-coverage verdicts are always emitted from the bank; zero banked verdicts remain a typed error signal, closing the verdict-less trap.
